Lewis Hamilton Claims Ferrari Pole in Mexico as Kimi Antonelli Closes on F1 History

01 Nov 2026, 06:04 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Sports Desk · Source: www.bbc.co.uk

Hamilton Secures Milestone Pole Position

Lewis Hamilton claimed his first Grand Prix pole position since the 2023 Hungarian Grand Prix during Saturday's qualifying session at the Mexico City Grand Prix. Driving for Ferrari, the seven-time world champion edged out his former Mercedes team-mate George Russell by just 0.009 seconds.

The result marks Hamilton's 105th career pole and his first since joining Ferrari. Speaking after the session, Hamilton described the achievement as one of the greatest feelings of his career, highlighting the journey of adapting to a new team alongside his engineers.

The Championship Equation for Kimi Antonelli

Meanwhile, 20-year-old Italian driver Kimi Antonelli faces a historic weekend as he stands on the brink of securing his maiden world championship. If successful, he would become the youngest champion in Formula 1 history.

  • Starting Position: Antonelli qualified fifth fastest, but a one-place grid penalty for Max Verstappen moves him up to the second row alongside Charles Leclerc.
  • Title Scenarios: Antonelli needs only to finish ninth if Russell wins the race, or 10th if Hamilton takes the victory, to seal the title.
  • Tactical Challenges: The run to the first corner in Mexico exceeds 800 metres, presenting both an opportunity for slipstreaming and a risk of first-corner incidents.

Driver Reflections and Practical Outlook

Antonelli admitted that the high stakes have weighed on him over the weekend, noting that he felt more tense than usual and struggled to keep his emotions flat.

Lewis Hamilton and George Russell acknowledged the strong likelihood of Antonelli securing the title. However, Hamilton noted that his own team's focus remains on scoring the best possible result and holding onto second place in the constructors' championship.

Fans looking to verify race outcomes and official standings can consult the official Formula 1 website or official broadcaster announcements for post-session reports and race classifications.
